OFFICE cy THE CLERK
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES
STEVEN WARD, Applicant/Pefitioner,
NYT OWNER, LLC
(as substituted for THOS. D. WALSH, INC., REALTORS), Respondent.
No. 25-6967
RENEWED EMERGENCY APPLICATION FOR STAY OF EXECUTION
PENDNG REVIEW OF INTERLOCUTORY AND FINAL ORDERS
To the Honorable John G. Roberts, Jr., Chief Justice of the United States and
Circuit Justice for the District of Columbia:
Applicant Steven Ward respectfully renews his emergency application for a stay of
execution of the April 14, 2026, Judgrnent for Possession and disbursement of
registry fimds in Case No. 2024-LTB-010829, and the April 10, 2026, Order of the
District ofColumbia Court ofAppeals CaseNo. 26-CV-0138 following a "Review
RECEIVED
APR 29 2026

Vacuum" — a signed written order remains unavailable for appellate attachment,
while a Writ of Restitution has been issued for immediate eviction.
1. JURISDICTION The jurisdiction ofthis Court is invoked under 28 U.S.C.
1257. Applicant seeks review of a final judgrnent and interlocutory orders from the
District ofColumbia Court of Appeals—the highest court oftheDistrict in which a
decision could be had—which has effectively insulated a trial court'sjurisdictional
errors from review. Applicant further moves for a stay pursuant to 28 U.S.C.
2101 (f) to prevent the irreparable harm of physical eviction and the irreversible
disbursement ofregistry funds before this Court can address the substantial federal
questions presented.
11. COMPLIANCE WITH RULE 23.3 (STATUS OF LOWER COURT
RELIEF)
In responseto the Clerk's letter dated April 24, 2026, Applicant clarifies that all
reasonable avenues for a stay in the lower courts have been exhausted or
effectively blocked by a "Review Vacuum." * Superior Court: On April 14,
2026, Applicant moved for an emergency stay, which was effectively iBlored as
the Court proceeded to enter Judgnent for Possession.
• D.C. Court of Appeals (DCCA): As evidenced by Exhibit E, Applicant
sought an emergency stay and filed a Notice of Jurisdictional Protest. The

DCCA's dismissal for lack of "finality" (Exhibit A), while the trial court
simultaneously executes a Writ of Restitution (Exhibit G), creates a
jurisdictional void where execution is immediate but judicial review is
structurally impossible.
m. JUDGMENTS TO BE REVIEWED
• April 10, 2026, DCCA Order (Exhibit A): This order dismissed
Applicant' s appeal for lack of finality while authorizing the retroactive
substitution of Respondent NYT Owner, LLC, despite the underlying
complaint being void ab initio for failure to comply with D.C. Code 16-
• April 14, 2026, Judgment for Possession (Exhibit B): The trial court
entered a "Redeemable Judgnentt' while refilsing to issuethe siY1ed, writtQ
order required to perfect an appeal. The procedural confusion is confirmed
by Exhibit C (Notice of Trial), which continued to caption the case under
the original, non-standing entity, and Exhibit D (Notice of Judgrnent),
which was mailed to "No Known Address," illustrating the breakdown of
due process.

lv. ARGUMENT FOR STAY
1. Jurisdictional Fraud and Standing Defects. The underlying case lacked the
mandatoryregistration required by D.C. Code 16-1501 at its inception. The
trial court's own record reflects this instability; Exhibit C proves that as ofthe trial
date, the court was still proceeding underthe name ofthe original Plaintiff, yet the
judgment was entered for a substituted entity. This "bait-and-switch" of parties on
the day of judgment facilitates the unauthorized practice of law and bypasses
jurisdictionalprerequisites. Theunderlyingjudgnent is void ab initio. Under D.C.
Code 16-1501 (c)(l), mandatory registration is a condition precedent to the
court' s subject matter jurisdiction. As argued in Applicant's Jurisdictional Protest,
the Respondent failed to satis$'theserequirements at the case's inception. A court
acting without subject matter jurisdiction possesses no power to issue a Writ of
Restitution; to allow such a writ to be executed violates the fundamental princip le
that jurisdictional defects may be challenged at any stage of proceedings.
2. The "Review Vacuum" and DueProcess. The central issueis whether a court
violates the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment by executing a
judgment while withholding the formal written order necessary to perfect an
appeal. Here, the U.S. Marshal has been commanded to execute an eviction
(Exhibit G) based on a docket entry thattheDCCA refuses to recoglize as a "final

order" for purposes of appeal. This places Applicant in a position where his
property and possessory interests are seized before any appellate court has
reviewed the underlying merits or jurisdiction. The "Review Vacuum" is not a
mere delay; it is a physical barrier evidenced by Exhibit D. While the trial court
claims ajudgment was "entered" tojusti$' an eviction, it has withheld the formal
signed order. The DCCA then uses this lack ofa signed order to deny review
(Exhibit A), while the Marshalproceeds with the Writ of Restitution (Exhibit G).
This denies Applicant the right to be heard "at a meaningåll time and in a
manner. "
3. Irreparable Harm and Registry Mismatch. Applicant faces imminent
physical eviction and the final disbursement of $6,600.00 from the court registry.
As shown in ExhibitF, these funds are being released to a substituted entity (NYT
Owner, LLC) that was not the party of record when the åmds were deposited.
Absent a stay, the Applicant's property and possessory interests will be seized
before any appellate courthas the opportunity to address the trial court's lack of
subject matterjurisdiction. This disbursement facilitates the unauthorized practice
of law and ensures that, even if Applicant eventually prevails on the merits, the
funds will have been transferred to a substituted entity, rendering recovery diffcult
or impossible.

V. CONCLUSION The nature oflandlord-tenant proceedings cannot
override the constitutional requirement of due process. Because the lower courts
have created a procedural environment where executionprecedes the possibility of
review, the intervention ofthis Court is the only remaining safeguard. Applicant
respectfully requests an immediate stay of the Writ of Restitution and the
disbursement of registry funds.
Respectfully submitted,
WanzL
/s/ teven Ward
Applicant Pro Se

DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA

BEFORE: Beckwith, Easterly, and Shanker, Associate Judges.
ORDER
On consideration of appellant's response (filed in Superior Court) to this
court's March 19, 2026, order directing him to show cause why this appeal should
not be dismissed as taken from nonfinal orders: appellant' s emergency motion for a
stay, which the March 19, 2026, order denied in part and held in abeyance in part;
appellant's combined motion to supplement the record and renewed emergency
motion for a stay; appellant's various "notices"; and appellant's motion for leave to
file a lodged supplemental notice; and it appearing that NYT Owner, LLC, has been
substituted as the plaintiff below, it is
ORDERED that NYT Owner, LLC, is subsåtuted for Thos. D. Walsh, Inc.,
Realtors, as the appellee in this matter- It is
FURTHER ORDERED that appellant's motion for leave to file the lodged
supplemental notice is granted and the Clerk shall file the lodged notice. It is
FURTHER ORDERED that appellant's combined motion to supplement the
record and renewed emergency motion for a stay is denied to the extent appellant
seeks to supplement the record- It is
FURTHER ORDERED that appellant's stay motions are denied. See Bany
v. Wash. Post co., 529 A.2d 319, 321 (D.C. 1987) (explaining that to prevail on a
motion for stay, the movant must that he is likely to succeed on the

No. 26-CV-0138
merits of the appeal; irreparable harm will result if the stay is denied; the opposing
party will not be harmed by the stay; and a stay would be in the public interest); see
also FTCv. Dean Foods co., 384 U.S. 597, 603 (1966) (explaining that the All Writs
Act, 28 U.S.C 1651 (a), empowers appellate courts to issue writs appropriate in aid
of their jurisdiction); A.C. v. N. W., 160 A.3d 509, 524 n.22 (D.C. 2017) (noting that
the All Writs Act applies to "all courts established by Act of Congress" including
the D.C. courts). It is
FURTHER ORDERED that the appeal is dismissed as having been taken from
nonfinal and nonappealable orders ofthe Superior Court. See D.C. Code I I -721 (a)
(stating this court has jurisdiction over appeals from 'Call final orders and judgments
of the Superior Court of the District of Columbia" and "interlocutory orders .
granting, continuing, modifying, refusing, or dissolving or refusing to dissolve or
modify injunctions"); Rolinski v. Lewis, 828 A.2d 739, 745-46 (D.C. 2003)
("Normally, an order or judgment is deemed to be final only if it disposes of the
whole case on its merits so that the court has nothing remaining to do but to execute
the judgment or decree already rendered." (citations and internal quotation marks
omitted)). An appeal may be taken after an adverse final judgment of the Superior
Court.
PER CURIAM
